chapter: The union and the 1920s-30s band scene
title: Bumps Meyers, tenor player with Les Hite
summary: Howard calls Meyers a very fine tenor player who started on alto and did solo work in Les Hite's band.

blocks.x: Well, you helped me get into the union, I remember that. So thanks a lot. Here's another player, too, of that period, Bumps Meyers.
Bumps Meyers? Yeah, he's dead now.
Well, yeah, he's dead, but he was a fine tenor player.
Very fine. Very fine tenor player.
Do you know much about his early musical career or what his studies were? I met him -- or, I possibly when he was with saw him (inaudible) Les Hite's band. But I don't know much about him.
Well, no. The first time I met Les --
Bumps. The first time I met Bumps, it was with the - not Les, (inaudible). Bumps was playing with the -- I'm trying to get to who he was playing with, now. I can't think who it was, but he played --
Was he an alto player at one point or --
And what about the period with Les? Was he like a featured soloist or anything like that? Because apparently that seemed to be his thing in later years.
He did a lot of solos.
